issues.t: Clutch actuator failure (car won't shift or move)
issues.sym: The car suddenly won't select a gear, gets stuck in neutral or one gear, shows a transmission warning, or won't move from a stop. It may slip first, on and off, before failing completely.
issues.why: This generation uses an automated manual gearbox: a regular clutch worked by an electric clutch actuator motor and a computer. The actuator motor and its shaft wear out or break, and corrosion from water can kill it.
issues.next: Stop driving if it won't hold a gear. A shop that knows smart cars should test the actuator before replacing the clutch or the whole gearbox; a used or rebuilt actuator is also an option.

issues.t: Won't go into reverse or stuck in neutral
issues.sym: Reverse sometimes won't engage, most often on the first start of the day or when warm. The display may show N with a warning beep, and the car can get stuck in neutral.
issues.why: The transmission control software and the clutch adjustment are often to blame. Many owners were fixed with a software update and a resync of the shifter; others needed a new clutch plate.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or smart specialist for the latest transmission software and a clutch relearn first. If that doesn't help, have the clutch plate and actuator checked.

issues.t: Clutch slipping or worn clutch plate
issues.sym: The engine revs up without the car speeding up, jerky or choppy shifts, or the car hesitates to move off.
issues.why: The automated gearbox still uses a dry clutch plate that wears out, and the computer-controlled engagement can wear it faster. German breakdown data showed clutch problems peaking on 2008-2009 cars.
issues.next: Have the clutch checked and the transmission software updated. If the plate is worn, replace it along with any damaged actuator parts.

issues.t: Gear selector sticks in Park or won't shift
issues.sym: The shift lever is stiff, stuck in Park, the shift button jams, or the car won't leave Park even with the brake pressed.
issues.why: The shifter mechanism can stick from dirt or lack of grease, and a faulty brake light switch can stop the car from letting you shift out of Park.
issues.next: Check that the brake lights work. A shop can often clean and lubricate the shifter; a worn shifter or brake switch can be replaced.

issues.t: Water leaks damaging transmission electronics
issues.sym: Damp carpets or water in the cabin, followed by shifting faults or a car that won't select gears.
issues.why: Water getting into the car can reach the transmission control unit and the clutch actuator, shorting or corroding them.
issues.next: Find and seal the water leak first. Then have the transmission electronics and actuator checked for corrosion.

issues.t: Engine misfire from failed ignition coils
issues.sym: The engine shakes or runs rough, feels down on power, and the check engine light may flash.
issues.why: The ignition coils on the 1.0L engine fail, and some owners have had to replace them more than once.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Engine compartment fire risk from loose insulation mat (recall)
issues.sym: A check engine light, smoke or a burning smell from the rear engine area. Fires reported to NHTSA spread quickly.
issues.why: The insulation mat in the rear engine compartment can deform, break down and come loose, then touch hot exhaust parts. NHTSA had looked into reports of 2008-2009 fortwos catching fire; the fix is recall 18V-273.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have a dealer check the VIN and install the improved mat for free.

issues.t: Windshield and roof bond paint defect (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In rare cases the paint where the windshield and roof are glued could let go while driving.
issues.why: A batch of paint did not meet spec, and repainted areas could peel at the windshield and roof adhesive joint (recall 08V-390, a small number of early 2008 cars).
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN to confirm the repaint was done.

issues.t: Steering gear mounting bolts can break (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or looseness in the steering, or steering that feels vague or pulls.
issues.why: The bolts that hold the steering gear to the car can break while driving (recall 15V-192). It includes 2014 electric drive cars.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN and replace the bolts free. If the steering feels loose, don't drive it.

issues.t: Parking brake may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake lever pulls up higher than usual, and the car may creep or roll when parked on a slope.
issues.why: A lock nut on the parking brake cable can loosen, so the brake loses holding force (recall 17V-448).
issues.next: Have a dealer replace the nut free. Until then, park on level ground and leave the car in Park.

issues.t: Headlight aim can be knocked out of spec (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights that seem aimed off to one side, or oncoming drivers flashing you.
issues.why: The sideways headlight adjuster wasn't sealed, so the beams can be set outside the federal standard (recall 17V-179).
issues.next: Have a dealer install the sealing caps free and check the headlight aim.

issues.t: Left front steering knuckle may crack (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. If the part fails, steering and control of the car can be affected.
issues.why: Some left front steering knuckles from one batch had casting flaws and could break (recall 17V-447).
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN and inspect or replace the knuckle free.

issues.t: Heater and A/C fan stops working
issues.sym: No air from the vents on some or all fan speeds, or the fan works only now and then.
issues.why: The HVAC blower motor wears out; its brushes can fail. It is the most common repair in TrueDelta's survey of fortwo owners.
issues.next: Have the blower motor and its resistor and wiring tested. Replacing the motor usually fixes it.

issues.t: Starter failure (click or no crank)
issues.sym: You turn the key and hear a click or nothing, while the dash lights still work.
issues.why: The starter motor fails on these years, and corroded starter wiring or ground straps can cause the same symptom. German breakdown data flags starters on 2008-2010 cars.
issues.next: Have the battery, starter wiring and ground strap checked before replacing the starter.

issues.t: Alternator failure or overcharging
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, lights dim or flicker, or the car stalls and won't restart because the battery goes flat.
issues.why: The alternator can fail or overcharge, and some replacement parts have been hard to find.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. Replace the alternator if its output is too low or too high.

issues.t: Weak 12V battery causing odd warnings or no start
issues.sym: Slow cranking or a dead car, sometimes with a check engine light or a rough-running engine before it fails.
issues.why: The 12V battery in these small cars wears out, and a weak one can cause strange warning lights. Electric versions also rely on a 12V battery, which smart says to replace about every three years.
issues.next: Have the battery tested first when odd warnings appear. Replace it with the correct type if it is weak.

issues.t: Exhaust flex pipe or muffler failure
issues.sym: A louder exhaust, rattling or buzzing from under the back of the car, or an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The flex pipe, middle pipe and muffler crack or rust through; it is one of the more common repairs in owner surveys, and later cars also show early rust on the tailpipe and heat shields.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected for leaks. Fix leaks soon so fumes don't get into the cabin.

issues.t: Check engine light from secondary air injection pump
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with a whirring noise right after a cold start.
issues.why: The secondary air pump, which blows air into the exhaust on cold starts to cut emissions, can fail.
issues.next: Have the code read. The car usually runs fine, but it needs fixing to pass an emissions test.

issues.t: Squealing drive belt
issues.sym: A squeal or whine from the engine, often at startup and especially on cars with the auto start-stop system.
issues.why: The accessory drive belt or its tensioner wears. German breakdown data reports belt failures on many years of this generation.
issues.next: Have the belt and tensioner checked and replaced if worn. A broken belt stops the alternator from charging.

issues.t: Engine oil leaks on older cars
issues.sym: Oil spots under the rear of the car or an oil smell, often found at inspection.
issues.why: Seals and gaskets on older 1.0L engines start to leak with age.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and have the source of the leak found. These engines have a small oil capacity, so running low happens quickly.

issues.t: A/C leaks that are hard to find
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm and needs recharging again and again.
issues.why: Refrigerant leaks are common and can be hard to pin down; compressors and condensers have also failed on some cars.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested with dye or a sniffer before paying for another recharge.

issues.t: Headlight bulbs burning out often
issues.sym: One headlight goes out, sometimes the same side again and again.
issues.why: Owners in TrueDelta's survey report frequent headlight bulb replacements on these cars.
issues.next: Replace the bulb with the correct type. If the same one keeps failing, have the connector and wiring checked.

issues.t: ABS warning light from a failed wheel speed sensor
issues.sym: The ABS and traction warning lights come on. The regular brakes still work.
issues.why: A wheel speed sensor fails or its wiring is damaged, so the anti-lock system shuts off.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read to find which wheel's sensor failed. Brake with extra care on slippery roads until it is fixed.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning from failed TPMS sensors
issues.sym: The tire pressure light stays on even though the tires are inflated correctly.
issues.why: A tire pressure sensor or its valve stem fails; valve stems show up often in owner repair reports.
issues.next: Check all tires with a gauge first. A tire shop can find and replace the bad sensor.

issues.t: Airbag light from seat or seatbelt sensor faults
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on, or the passenger airbag off light behaves oddly.
issues.why: Loose connectors at the seat weight sensor and failed seatbelt tensioners or sensors have triggered airbag faults on these cars.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read soon. The airbags may not work correctly while the light is on.

issues.t: Turbocharger damage on the 0.9L turbo
issues.sym: Loss of power, rough running, whistling, or blue smoke from the exhaust.
issues.why: Turbo damage is described as a fairly common and serious problem on the 0.9L turbo engine used in the newer fortwo.
issues.next: Use the correct oil and change it on time, and let the engine idle briefly after hard driving. Have power loss checked quickly.

issues.t: Rough running or stalling from worn sensors and valves
issues.sym: The engine stumbles or stutters, the check engine light comes on, and in some cases the car stalls or won't start.
issues.why: Worn oxygen (lambda) sensors and solenoid valves are reported causes of rough running on the newer fortwo.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the codes read so the specific sensor or valve can be replaced.

issues.t: Electric drive won't charge (charging unit failure)
issues.sym: The car won't take a charge when plugged in, or charging stops early, sometimes with a warning light.
issues.why: Owners of the electric drive version have reported failures of the on-board charging unit.
issues.next: Try another charger to rule out the station. A smart or Mercedes dealer with high-voltage training needs to diagnose the car; check whether battery and EV warranty coverage still applies.
